# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the

Let me map who can reach whom before I send anything.

- **Me (Mute):** I can gesture — but only Deaf receives gestures. I can hear, so I can receive speech from Blind and Deaf. I can never reach Blind with content: he can't see gestures, and I can't speak. Blind is permanently out of my range.
- **Deaf:** sees the bomb (light colour, wires) and my gestures; cannot hear, but nothing stops Deaf from speaking — and Blind and I can both hear.
- **Blind:** the only one who can touch the bomb, and the only one who can speak and be heard... but actually Deaf can speak too. Either way, whatever reaches Blind's hands must travel through someone's voice, and the only bridge from my manual to a voice is Deaf.

So Deaf is the hub: manual (me, gestures) → Deaf → voice → Blind's hands.

What I hold: the light walks a fixed circle of three colours, and the wire to cut depends on the colour shown at the moment of the cut. So far the manual shows exactly one row: **orange light → cut yellow wire**. Deaf can see the light directly, so Deaf doesn't need me to describe colours — Deaf needs the *mapping*. But gestures carry no inherent meaning, and a wrong guess detonates the bomb, so I won't try to encode "orange" and "yellow" arbitrarily. Instead I'll open the only channel that is self-correcting: a conventional yes/no code. 👋 gets attention, then 👍 = yes, 👎 = no. Deaf can then ask questions out loud (I can hear; the questions reach me at the start of next round), and I answer in ordered thumbs. Deaf can batch several yes/no questions per turn, so this is slow but safe and verifiable.

Once yes/no is confirmed, the questions I want Deaf to ask are: "does the light colour decide the wire?", "is the first row orange→yellow?", "is that the only row you have?", and then Deaf can time the order to Blind so the cut lands while the light is orange — until more manual pages arrive, that's the only colour I can vouch for.

Opening move: establish attention and the yes/no convention with Deaf, addressed to Deaf alone (to Blind it would be meaningless noise anyway).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. My hands found: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. I can only cut wires, by position. Colours and printing never reach me, and I never receive gestures, so right now I know nothing beyond that layout. Check the manual for how display, light and wire colours decide the cut. Remember: you cannot speak and I cannot see gestures, so the only path to me is Deaf's voice. Gesture the rules to Deaf; Deaf can speak and I can hear. I am gesturing to Deaf now to ask for the readouts aloud: display, light, then wire colours in order 1, 2, 3.
Blind gestures: [🫵 🤙 👆 👇 👈 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👋]
Deaf says: Bomb report, for both of you: the display reads 0. The light is orange. There are three wires. Left to right: wire one is red, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. There are no other markings or readings on it. Mute, look up what the manual says for this and sign me the instruction. Blind, you have the full picture now from hearing this; the instruction will come from my mouth once Mute signs it to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I received your wave, thumb up and thumb down. Code proposal: one finger means wire one, two fingers means wire two, the sign with thumb, index and pinky means wire three. Thumb up means yes or correct, thumb down means no. Wave first to get my attention, then sign the instruction.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The code is set — Deaf proposed it and confirmed with a thumbs-up, so the vocabulary is live: ☝/✌/🤟 for wires 1/2/3, 👍/👎 for yes/no.

Now the defusal logic. Deaf's report and Blind's exploration agree: display reads 0, light is orange, wires red–yellow–blue at positions 1–2–3. My manual has exactly one row: **orange light → cut yellow wire**. Yellow is position 2. So the instruction is ✌ — cut wire 2.

Timing is the one risk: the light changes every round, and only the light at the moment of the cut matters. The light is orange right now, and Deaf sees it live — Deaf must watch it and have Blind cut while it still shows orange, this round. My single manual row gives no rule for any other colour, so this instruction is only valid under orange.

Wave to get attention, then the instruction, then thumbs-up as confirmation: "wire 2, confirmed, go." I'll keep it addressed to Deaf alone.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✌", "👍"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. I heard Deaf's report and I pass it to you in full, since you need the bomb state to pick the right manual rule. Display shows the digit 0. Light is orange. Wires, left to right: one red, two yellow, three blue. Nothing else is printed anywhere. My only possible action is cutting one wire at position 1, 2 or 3. Channel map: you hear me and Deaf, but you can only answer by gesture. Deaf hears nobody, so Deaf lives on gestures from you and me, and Deaf can speak to both of us. So the plan: find the rule covering display 0, orange light, red/yellow/blue wires, and boil it down to a single wire position. Keep whatever you sign to Deaf simple: numbers and yes/no checks, so Deaf can verify against the visible bomb and speak me one number. I have just defined a small code to both of you by gesture: fingers for one, two, three; a pinch for cut; thumbs for yes and no.
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤏 👍 👎 🫵 🤏 ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Deaf says: Update for both of you: the light has changed from orange to green since my last report. The display still reads 0, and all three wires are untouched — red on the left, yellow in the middle, blue on the right. Mute, I received your signs: wave, wire two, yes. Before anyone acts, I need the verb. New code: the OK sign means cut, the fist means press, and thumb-down alone at the end of a message means it is a question. So: is the instruction to cut wire two? And does the light turning green change the manual's answer — thumb-up if cutting wire two still stands, thumb-down if I should expect new signs. Blind, Mute's message concerns wire two, which is the MIDDLE wire of the three you can feel — you cannot see that it is yellow, but it is the one in the middle of your hand. Do not cut or press anything yet. Confirm by feel instead: sign the three-finger sign if you clearly feel a middle wire, and sign anything else you can about what your hands find — I have only told you what I see; whatever your fingers discover, only you can report.

The critical fact this round: **the light is green now, and my manual has no rule for green.** The only row I hold is orange → yellow. Deaf asked me directly: thumb-up if "cut wire two" still stands, thumb-down if new signs are coming. Honest answer: thumb-down — under green, cutting is unsupported by everything I have. If Deaf took my round-2 order as still live and had Blind cut now, we'd be acting on nothing.

But I must prevent the opposite misread — that "new signs are coming" means "cut wire 2 anyway, now." So the headline of my new signs is HOLD. I'll spend ✋ as a new sign meaning wait/hold: it's the most universally readable stop gesture, and even if Deaf misparses it, no reading of it triggers a cut — worst case Deaf asks what it means, and the question-marker protocol (lone 👎 at the end) lets us settle it next round. Meanwhile the standing order was already "nobody acts yet," so a slower clarification costs time, not the bomb.

Then I re-anchor the target with redundancy: not wire 1, not wire 3, yes wire 2 — the middle of the three Blind feels. Note I'm ending every multi-sign message with 👍, never a trailing lone 👎, so nothing I send can be mistaken for a question.

What I deliberately do *not* try: signing colours (I have no referents for orange/green — the wire colours red/yellow/blue don't overlap), or signing "the circle of three repeats" (unsignable without noise; Deaf watches the light live and will see the cycle directly). The timing problem is real — Deaf's voice reaches Blind a round late, so Deaf must learn the light's rhythm and pre-call the cut so it lands in an orange window — but Deaf has all the visual data needed to solve that once it knows "cut wire 2, only under orange." I expect Deaf's next move to be exactly that yes/no question, and I'll confirm with 👍.

Answer first, then headline, then exclusivity:

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✋", "✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎", "🤟", "👎", "✌", "👍"])
```

One: the light is RED right now — recheck the manual and tell me if red changes the instruction. Two: sign the verb from this menu — OK sign means cut wire two, fist means press wire two, flat hand means hold wire two pressed down, pointing finger means tap wire two once. If none of these, thumb-down and I will offer more. Three: does the manual say what the display count or the light colors mean — thumb-up if yes and then describe it with our signs, thumb-down if no.

The picture is nearly complete. Deaf has now observed the full cycle: orange → green → red. My manual says the light "always walks the same circle of three colours," so that observed order **is** the circle, and it will return to orange. My table has exactly one row — orange → yellow (wire 2) — so green and red mean *no cut, wait*. Nothing in the manual keys on the display at all, so the 0 means nothing so far. Crucially, no one has stated any timer: the only death is a wrong action, so patience is free and I will not push Deaf to hurry a cut.

Deaf asked three questions in a fixed order; I answer in that order, with two safety rules of my own: no message of mine names an action without its condition, and I retire my round-3 flat-hand sign — Deaf just redefined ✋ as "hold wire pressed down," an action I never sanctioned, so I'm introducing 🙏 as WAIT instead and will never use ✋ again.

**Message 1 (red):** I lead with the new WAIT sign before any yes/no, so even if Deaf misparses the 👎 ("no red row exists"), the actionable takeaway is *do nothing under red* — the polarity trap from last round can't trigger a cut.

**Message 2 (verb):** From Deaf's menu I pick 👌 = cut, with ✌ wire-two attached redundantly: "the armed instruction is CUT WIRE 2." Arming is safe; only Deaf's voice can execute, and Deaf won't speak the go until it has the condition.

**Message 3 (the rule):** Blind asked for a full table; here it is. I introduce 🫳 as a topic frame meaning "the light," then number the colours **by the order Deaf itself reported seeing them**: ☝ = first-seen (orange) → 👌✌ cut wire 2; ✌ = second-seen (green) → 🙏 wait; 🤟 = third-seen (red) → 🙏 wait. Deaf can verify the circle empirically by watching for orange to return. If the numbering basis is unclear, Deaf's question protocol (lone trailing 👎) settles it next round — and I never end a message with a lone 👎, so nothing I send reads as a question by accident.
